title: Harden Rename WebView apply safety feedback
summary: Improve Rename tab operator feedback for checked-only apply scope, duplicate-target blocking, confirmation clarity, result-modal evidence, and bad-case logging feedback.
reason: The Rename tab audit found that unchecked fallback apply scope, duplicate-target presentation, modal copy, stale result evidence, and status colors could make filesystem mutation look too casual or ambiguous.
behavior_before: Rename Apply could visually imply all applicable rows would be applied when none were checked, duplicate targets were not urgent enough, result counts conflated applied rows with renamed files, and modal feedback did not clearly separate preview from mutation.
behavior_after: Rename Apply requires checked rows, Check Applicable skips warnings/blockers/duplicates/collisions with visible feedback, duplicate targets block readiness, confirmation lists exact checked paths and backend mutation boundary, result counts separate renamed/unchanged/skipped/protected/failed, and bad-case append feedback remains visible.
manual_validation: git diff --check -- [Rename WebView/test files] - passed with line-ending normalization warnings only
rollback_plan: Revert the Rename WebView JS/CSS/HTML changes, targeted smoke/static test updates, and this change packet.
notes:
WebView feedback and smoke validation only. The frontend still posts rename.apply only through the backend and this work does not process media, save settings, mutate queue state, apply filesystem renames, or touch source/output/scratch media.
Implemented checked-only Rename apply safety feedback and validated targeted smokes.
